newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan construction firms up on spending hopes.
newsitem.headline: Japan construction firms up on spending hopes.

text.p: Shares in the construction sector were higher on Friday afternoon, spurred on by hopes that the new government formed after Sunday's elections will step up public spending once it comes to office, brokers said.

As of 0440 GMT, Taisei Corp was up 11 yen at 725 yen, in a volume of 1.177 million shares. Shimizu Corp was up 10 yen at 1,110 yen on a volume of 1.312 million. Kajima Corp was up 30 yen at 1,070 yen on a 1.423 million turnover.
Tobishima Corp was 31 yen higher at 447 yen.
Brokers said that on top of the election hopes, a newspaper report that Tobishima and Fuji Bank had agreed on a new restructuring plan for the firm was lifting the shares.
"We would like to have a news conference or to release a comment to clarify our stance about today's newspaper report," a Tobishima spokesman said.
Tobishima said it may hold a news conference about its restructuring plan at around 4.30 p.m. (0730 GMT).

Media reports said earlier that the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), the biggest party in the current coalition government, will press for a five trillion yen supplementary budget by the end of the calendar year.
Brokers said the report was encouraging market participants to buy related issues that would benefit from more public expenditure, such as construction companies as well as real estate developers.
Recent media polls show that the LDP could secure a simple majority in the election for the 500-seat Lower House of parliament on Sunday.
